title: What If Africa Split in Two?

scenes.text: What if Africa split in two? It's already happening, and a new ocean is coming.
Under East Africa, tectonic plates are slowly pulling apart along a long valley called the East African Rift.
In 2005, a crack about thirty-five miles long opened in Ethiopia's Afar desert, over roughly ten days.
The Nubian and Somali plates drift apart slowly, roughly five to thirteen millimeters a year.
Eventually, seawater from the Red Sea could flood the rift and form a brand new ocean basin.
That takes at least five to ten million years. But the ocean is already on its way.
